scenario: WIBTA if I told my cousin his kid can’t stay in our house? | My cousin (M27) recently moved in with my husband and I. We completely closed of the very large main bedroom and bathroom to create a flatlet for him that’s separate from the house with his own entrance so it’s basically two separate units of one house. Now my cousin has a 2 year old and he’s busy with a custody battle with his ex so he can get to spend more time with his son. I completely support this and really hopes he gets more time with his son. Yesterday my cousin came to ask me if it would be possible for my husband and I to convert our spare bedroom into a room for his son if and when he comes to visit over weekends. There is no access from my cousin’s room into our part of the house and he doesn’t have keys to come and go as he pleases. I understand that the court will be looking into his living situation to see if he has suitable space for his son to stay with him (and to be honest his current room and bathroom is more than big enough) but I’m not comfortable with letting his son sleep in our house if my cousin has no access to him and I’m not willing to take responsibility for his kid. The whole family is involved in this because that’s just the way my family is and everyone expects me to help out my cousin with his current custody situation to get him more time with his son. WIBTA for telling him I will not allow his son to sleep in our house and completely jeopardizing his court case?

He has a 2-year-old son, and he's going through a custody battle with his ex. I really support him wanting to spend more time with his son, and I hope he gets more visitation rights. Yesterday, he asked if we could convert our spare bedroom into a room for his son, so that when he comes over for weekends, his son can stay there. But here's the thing: there's no access from my cousin's room into our part of the house, and he doesn't have keys to come and go as he pleases. I'm not comfortable letting his son sleep in our house if my cousin can't access him, and I'm not willing to take responsibility for his kid. The whole family is involved in this because that's just how my family is, and everyone expects me to help out my cousin with his current custody situation to get him more time with his son. Now, I'm wondering if I should tell him I won't allow his son to sleep in our house, which could jeopardize his court case. I need to think about whether it's right or wrong for me to say no. On one hand, I want to support my cousin and help him get more time with his son. On the other hand, I'm not comfortable with the idea of his son staying in our house without my cousin having access, and I don't want to take on the responsibility for his child. Maybe I should consider the legal implications. If the court is looking into his living situation to see if he has suitable space for his son, then having a separate room in our house might help his case. But if I refuse to let his son stay here, it could make it look like he doesn't have a stable place for his son, which might not be good for his custody case. I also need to think about the family dynamics. Everyone expects me to help out, and if I say no, it might cause tension within the family. But I also have to respect my own boundaries and comfort levels. It's important for me to feel safe and secure in my own home, and I don't want to compromise that just to help someone else. Perhaps I can find a middle ground. Maybe instead of converting our spare bedroom, we can find another arrangement that still allows his son to stay in a separate space without giving him access to our part of the house. Or maybe we can set up some kind of monitored access where he can visit his son without being able to come and go freely. I also need to communicate my concerns clearly to my cousin. He needs to understand why I'm hesitant and maybe work together to find a solution that works for everyone. It's important to maintain a good relationship with him, but I also need to prioritize my own comfort and security. In the end, I have to decide what feels right for me. If I can't be comfortable with his son staying in our house under the current conditions, then it might be better to say no, even if it affects his custody case. But I also don't want to be the reason he loses more time with his son. It's a tough situation, and I wish there was an easier way to handle it.
